description: Me, Myself & MODIS is an independent project focused on making satellite-based fire intelligence more accessible and reliable. We aim to harmonise NASA's MODIS and VIIRS active-fire observations, investigate sensor differences, and explore historical fire activity across Pakistan. Through data analysis, remote sensing and interactive visualisation, our goal is to turn complex Earth observation data into meaningful environmental insights.
summary: FireTrace Pakistan harmonizes NASA FIRMS MODIS and VIIRS fire hot-spot observations over Pakistan from 2000 to 2026. MODIS (about 1 km resolution, since 2000) and VIIRS (375 m, since 2012) report fires differently, so their raw counts cannot be compared directly. Our pipeline merges four FIRMS feeds into one schema, aggregates detections onto a shared 0.25° grid and weekly timeline, and normalizes activity within each sensor family. Each cell-week is then classified as seen by both sensors, MODIS only or VIIRS only, with a correlation of relative activity. The live dashboard offers an interactive map, sensor comparison, seasonality, ranked persistent and concentrated locations, and a CSV download of the harmonized data. It matters because researchers and analysts need a consistent way to compare the two satellite records before drawing conclusions about fire patterns. Counts are observations, not unique fires.
details:
FireTrace Pakistan is a live web dashboard for the NASA Space Apps challenge "Harmonization of MODIS and VIIRS Hot Spots".

What it does: A Python pipeline merges four NASA FIRMS feeds (MODIS, plus VIIRS on Suomi-NPP, NOAA-20 and NOAA-21, both archive and near-real-time) into one DuckDB database. Detections are aggregated onto a shared 0.25° grid and weekly timeline, then normalized per sensor family (detections per 100,000 detections of the same sensor that week). Each cell-week is classified as BOTH, MODIS_ONLY or VIIRS_ONLY, and we calculate a correlation of relative activity.

Benefits and impact: Researchers, disaster-management and agriculture analysts and students get a consistent basis for comparing the two satellite records, ranked locations that burn year after year, seasonal patterns, and a downloadable CSV of the harmonized weekly grid for any date range.

Tools: Python, Flask, DuckDB, Leaflet, JavaScript, HTML and CSS, hosted on PythonAnywhere. Code: https://github.com/BabarKhanD/firetrace-pakistan

What we considered: The dashboard states its limits. Counts are observations, not unique fires. Agreement between sensors does not prove they detected the same fire. Correlation measures similarity in relative spatial activity, not detection sensitivity.

AI assistance: Claude (Anthropic) was used to help write code, design the interface, and draft text.
